title: Thresholds
subtitle: The most specific set in force wins. An equipment override replaces the standard without changing it.

standards.title: Standards
standards.subtitle: Each standard carries its scale. A report (service order) picks its standard; if it picks none, each machine's own applies.
standards.noClasses: This standard does not classify by machine type

metric.inUseHint: with at least one band set

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.subtitle: Colour and name come from here; each technique picks which ones it offers.
statuses.availabilityHint: Declared by the technician; they explain why there is no value.
statuses.editHint: Its name, the severity it competes with, and what it implies

sets.title: Band sets
sets.hint: Listed from the most specific scope to the most general: the first one that matches an equipment wins.
sets.simulateResult: It decides {{points}} point(s): graded today, their latest readings would move {{count}} equipment(s) — {{detail}}
sets.cascade: The most specific wins, top to bottom
sets.retireBody: Readings already judged keep this criterion. New ones are judged by the next one in the cascade or, if there is none, stay unjudged.
sets.simulateSteady: It decides {{count}} point(s) and none would change status with its latest readings.
sets.simulateNone: It decides no reading today: a more specific criterion wins, or there are no readings of this magnitude.

form.standardHint: A standard judges the services it was written for. ISO 10816-3 is vibration; NETA MTS is thermography.
form.name: Name
form.sourceHint: Title or scope of the standard
form.techniquesHint: Pick none to make it a house criterion that applies to any service.
form.machineClassesHint: Optional: ISO 10816-3 uses Classes I to IV.
form.setHint: Pick the magnitude first: it fixes the service and therefore which standards may apply.
form.magnitudeHint: What is measured and in what unit
form.scopeHint: The most specific one in force wins
form.bandsHint: From (inclusive) to (exclusive). Leave empty for infinity. They cannot overlap.
form.rationaleHint: Why this criterion exists; it shows up in the report.
form.statusHint: Condition is computed from the value; availability is declared by the technician.
form.severityHint: Higher is worse; it orders the statuses
form.measurable: Can be measured in this state
form.magnitudeFormHint: A magnitude belongs to exactly one service.
form.aggregationHint: Gs peak and Gs peak-to-peak are different criteria
form.higherIsWorseHint: Viscosity and dielectric strength get worse as they drop
form.measurableHint: A machine that is off or retired is not measured

magnitudes.title: Measurement types
magnitudes.subtitle: What each service measures. The magnitude fixes the service and therefore which standards may judge it.
magnitudes.orderHint: Where its table sits in the record of values: the lowest number goes first.
magnitudes.templateOnlyHint: Read only on the points whose train-kind template lists it; elsewhere the round neither offers it nor counts it as not measured.
magnitudes.inRecordHint: Its table always shows in the record of values, with open cells in the service's rounds even before any reading.
magnitudes.confirmDelete: Delete this measurement? Only possible if it was never recorded and no threshold judges it.
magnitudes.serviceFixed: The service cannot change once created: its normas and readings hang off it.

explain.title: What is a measurement type?
explain.what: What a service measures, with its unit: vibration velocity in mm/s, temperature in °C, wall thickness in mm. Each measurement belongs to one service, which decides which normas may judge it.
explain.aggregation: The aggregation says how the signal is summarised: RMS, peak, peak to peak, average, maximum or minimum. “Envelope in gE peak” and “in gE peak to peak” are different criteria.
explain.order: “Order in the record”: where its table sits in the record of values and the reports; the lower number comes first.
explain.flags: “Fixed table”: its table always shows in the record, with open cells. “Template only”: measured only on the points whose train-kind template asks for it.
explain.example: Example — Vibration velocity · Vibration analysis · mm/s · RMS · 2 decimals · order 10 · higher is worse · fixed table

units.hint: The symbol is what appears next to the value in reports.
units.tableHint: The symbol printed next to every value in the reports
units.inUse: Cannot delete: magnitudes are reported in this unit
units.usedByHint: How many measurements are reported in this unit. With at least one, the unit cannot be deleted, and renaming it changes every report that uses it.

scale.title: Scale
scale.empty: No scale: this standard grades no magnitude yet.
scale.modalHint: The bands this standard grades a magnitude with. A report citing the standard is graded by them.
scale.bandsHint: From (included) to (excluded); empty means no limit. Statuses such as Alert are created in Statuses.

profiles.title: States per service
profiles.hint: Each service has its own set of states: which ones its norma may grade into and which ones the technician may declare instead of a value. A state can carry another name in that service only. What sets a machine with isolators apart from one without is not another service: it is other limits, in Thresholds.
profiles.modalHint: Tick the states this service uses. The own name is optional: “Medium” instead of “Alarm”, for example.
